bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is exactly four bytes: `01 0F 1B 01`. In `fuzz_disasmnext`, byte `0x01` selects `platforms[1] = { CS_ARCH_X86, CS_MODE_64 }`, so `cs_disasm()` receives instruction bytes `0F 1B 01`. The saved MSan path and the generated printer source together show that these bytes decode to internal opcode `X86_BNDSTXmr`, reaching `X86GenAsmWriter1.inc:32621-32623`, which prints the memory operand with `printanymem(MI, 0, O)` and then prints operand 5 with `printOperand(MI, 5, O)`. In the vulnerable revision, stack object `mci` carries field `x86opsize`, but `MCInst_Init()` never initializes that field and `printanymem()` only assigns `x86opsize` for `LEA*` opcodes. Because `X86_BNDSTXmr` falls through the switch default, `printMemReference()` copies the uninitialized `MI->x86opsize` into `MI->op1_size`, and the subsequent `if (MI->op1_size == 0)` in `printOperand()` reads that poisoned byte. The fix commit adds `X86_BNDSTXmr` and the related MPX BND opcodes to the size-setting switch so `x86opsize` is initialized before this path.

source.code: r = handle->disasm(ud, buffer, size, &mci, &insn_size, offset, handle->getinsn_info);
source.description: First project-code statement on the vulnerable path that consumes the attacker-controlled instruction bytes and materializes the decoded opcode/state in `mci`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` bytes are `01 0F 1B 01`. Harness line `suite/fuzz/fuzz_disasm.c:247` makes `Data[0] = 0x01` select `platforms[1] = { CS_ARCH_X86, CS_MODE_64 }`, so `cs_disasm()` receives `buffer = { 0x0F, 0x1B, 0x01 }`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: The stack `MCInst` object contains field `x86opsize` (`MCInst.h:98`). `MCInst_Init()` later clears many `MCInst` fields but never writes `x86opsize`, so this byte keeps indeterminate stack contents until some printer helper assigns it.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: MemorySanitizer reports the uninitialized value as created by allocation of `mci` in the stack frame of `cs_disasm`; the exact declaration is line 847.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. `printOperand()` reads `MI->op1_size`, which the immediately preceding `printMemReference()` call loaded from the still-uninitialized `MI->x86opsize`.
sink.note: The saved `reproduction_report.json` and `sanitizer_trace.txt` both identify `printOperand` at `arch/X86/X86IntelInstPrinter.c:822:7` as the use-of-uninitialized-value sink.

root_cause.description: For `X86_BNDSTXmr`, `printanymem()` takes the switch default and leaves `MI->x86opsize` untouched instead of assigning the correct 4-byte memory operand size.
root_cause.note: The vulnerable switch only handles `LEA16r`, `LEA32r`, `LEA64_32r`, and `LEA64r`. The patch adds `X86_BNDSTXmr` to the 4-byte arm and the related MPX BND opcodes to the 4-byte or 8-byte arms, closing this exact omission.

parser_admitted.code: size_t count = cs_disasm(handle, Data+1, Size-1, address, 0, &all_insn);
parser_admitted.description: The staged witness has `Data[0] = 0x01`, so line 247 selects `platforms[1] = { CS_ARCH_X86, CS_MODE_64 }`. The remaining three bytes `0F 1B 01` are then passed to `cs_disasm()` as one X86-64 instruction stream.

fine_trace.note: Initializes many `MCInst` fields before decoding, but `MCInst_Init()` only writes `Opcode`, `OpcodePub`, `size`, `has_imm`, `op1_size`, `writeback`, `ac_idx`, `popcode_adjust`, `assembly[0]`, and `wasm_data.type`. It never assigns `x86opsize`, so the `mci.x86opsize` byte inherited from the stack declaration at `cs.c:847` remains indeterminate.

fine_trace.code: r = handle->disasm(ud, buffer, size, &mci, &insn_size, offset, handle->getinsn_info);
fine_trace.note: Consumes the attacker-controlled bytes `0F 1B 01` and decodes them into `mci`. The later generated-printer frame at `X86GenAsmWriter1.inc:32621` identifies the resulting internal opcode as `X86_BNDSTXmr` for this witness.

The decoded `BNDSTXmr` instruction enters generated printer case 12. That case first prints the memory operand with `printanymem(MI, 0, O)` and then, on the same `MCInst`, prints operand 5 with `printOperand(MI, 5, O)`.

Because `MI->Opcode` is `X86_BNDSTXmr`, none of the `LEA*` cases match and the switch takes the default arm. `printanymem()` therefore does not assign `MI->x86opsize`, leaving it at the indeterminate stack value from step 1.

When the memory operand finishes printing, `printMemReference()` copies the still-uninitialized `MI->x86opsize` into `MI->op1_size`. The saved MSan trace names this exact assignment as the store site where the poisoned byte is written to memory before the crash.

MSAN sink. The same `BNDSTXmr` printer case from step 3 immediately calls `printOperand(MI, 5, O)`, and this branch reads the poisoned `MI->op1_size` byte propagated in step 5. MemorySanitizer reports the use-of-uninitialized-value at this read.

allocation_context.note: The sanitizer trace says the uninitialized value was created by allocation of `mci` in the stack frame of `cs_disasm`; the exact `MCInst mci;` declaration is line 847.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. MSan traces the poisoned byte to stack object `mci` in `cs_disasm`; `MCInst_Init()` leaves `x86opsize` undefined there, and `printanymem()` fails to overwrite it for `X86_BNDSTXmr`.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved stack is `printOperand -> X86_Intel_printInst -> cs_disasm`, and the fine trace fills in the intervening generated-printer `BNDSTXmr` case, `printanymem()`, and `printMemReference()` statements on that exact path.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch adds `X86_BNDSTXmr` and the related MPX BND opcodes to the `printanymem()` size switch in both Intel and AT&T printers, so `MI->x86opsize` is initialized to 4 or 8 before `printMemReference()` copies it to `op1_size`.

format.name: raw 4-byte Capstone fuzz_disasmnext witness
format.contract: A 4-byte input whose first byte is exactly `0x01`, selecting `platforms[1] = { CS_ARCH_X86, CS_MODE_64 }`, and whose remaining three bytes are exactly `0F 1B 01`. In the staged vulnerable build those bytes decode to internal opcode `X86_BNDSTXmr`, reach `X86GenAsmWriter1.inc:32621-32623`, and exercise the missing `printanymem()` size initialization that leaves `MI->x86opsize` uninitialized before it is copied into `MI->op1_size` and read in `printOperand()`. The verified trigger is this exact 4-byte witness, not a generalized class of all MPX instructions.
